lines.text: Mrs. Applegate stands on the gravel bar among the tolls. She doesn't come when called. She looks past Eldwin, back up the road.
Waiting for someone, are you. It isn't me.
Eldwin holds out Tilly's ribbon. Mrs. Applegate considers it for some time.
She lowers her head an inch, which is as far as she means to go, and lets him tie it on.
There. The left side of the road, Tilly said, and no cheese.
Mrs. Applegate sets off along the left side of the road, ahead of him, as if it had been her idea.
